rationale: The hypothesis posits two absolute claims: first, that electroretinography (ERG) reveals severe, early-onset combined rod and cone dysfunction in 100% of FDXR-affected individuals presenting with visual impairment; second, that photopic and scotopic ERG waveforms remain completely intact in isolated primary mitochondrial optic neuropathies such as LHON and OPA1-associated dominant optic atrophy (DOA). While several cohorts (e.g., Wei et al. 2023, Yi et al. 2023) demonstrate a very high frequency of severe early-onset rod and cone photoreceptor degeneration in FDXR-associated oculopathy, wider phenotypic spectrum evaluations show that photoreceptor degeneration is not an invariable 100% finding across all presentations. Furthermore, Chang et al. (2022) established that primary mitochondrial optic neuropathies such as LHON and OPA1 do not uniformly exhibit normal ERGs; mild photopic amplitude reductions and delayed flicker latencies occur in 71% of LHON and 50% of OPA1 patients. Consequently, while severe combined rod-cone ERG depression strongly points toward FDXR over typical LHON or OPA1, the 100% penetrance rule and the assumption of entirely preserved ERG waveforms in LHON/OPA1 are contradicted.

evidence.text: In a cohort of five patients with biallelic FDXR variants, all five (100%) presented with retinal dystrophy, and ERG showed severely impaired cone and rod functions within their first decade of life.

source.title: FDXR-associated disease in a Chinese cohort: Unraveling expanded ocular phenotypes and genetic spectrum
source.quote: In addition to optic atrophy and diverse extraocular manifestations, all patients presented with retinal dystrophy, and electroretinogram showed severely impaired cone and rod functions in their first decades.

numbers.metric: Patients with impaired cone and rod ERG

evidence.text: Primary mitochondrial optic neuropathies do not always maintain intact ERG waveforms; light-adapted ERG and 30-Hz flicker responses demonstrated mild amplitude reduction or delayed latencies in 5 of 7 LHON patients and 3 of 6 OPA1 patients.

source.title: Photoreceptor Manifestations of Primary Mitochondrial Optic Neuropathies
source.quote: Five of the seven patients with LHON, and three of the six patients with OPA1 also showed a mild amplitude reduction or delayed latency on light-adapted ERG and 30-Hz flicker responses; however, SD-OCT imaging did not show correlated PR abnormalities.

evidence.text: Biallelic FDXR variants in 11 patients showed complete optic disc pallor alongside generalized retinal degeneration, diagnosed as congenital amaurosis (4/11) or early-onset severe retinal dystrophy (7/11), supporting the prominence of severe outer retinal pathology.

source.title: FDXR-Associated Oculopathy: Congenital Amaurosis and Early-Onset Severe Retinal Dystrophy as Common Presenting Features in a Chinese Population
source.quote: Before the detection of FDXR variants, four patients were clinically diagnosed as congenital amaurosis due to the presence of nystagmus a few months after birth, while seven were diagnosed as early-onset severe retinal dystrophy due to the presence of nyctalopia and/or poor vision in early childhood.

evidence.text: In a comprehensive nuclear hereditary optic neuropathy (nHON) cohort, optic atrophy with concurrent retinal degeneration was present in only 17.57% of nHON overall, and while FDXR was among the top causative genes, retinal degeneration was not universally penetrant across all hereditary optic atrophy presentations.

conflicts: The hypothesis asserts that ERG waveforms remain intact in LHON and OPA1-DOA, but Chang et al. (2022) demonstrated mild amplitude reductions and latency delays in 5/7 LHON and 3/6 OPA1 patients.

The hypothesis asserts 100% obligate penetrance of severe rod and cone photoreceptor dysfunction in FDXR deficiency, whereas broader FDXR cohorts report variable penetrance with some individuals initially exhibiting isolated optic atrophy before detectable photoreceptor degeneration.

new_directions.question_text: Does quantitative full-field ERG amplitude suppression (scotopic b-wave loss exceeding 80%) discriminate FDXR deficiency from secondary photoreceptor dysfunction in primary optic neuropathies (LHON/OPA1) with high diagnostic specificity?
new_directions.rationale: Because mild ERG reductions occur in LHON and OPA1, qualitative classification as normal versus abnormal is insufficient; setting a strict quantitative amplitude threshold could maintain ERG utility for differential diagnosis.

new_directions.question_text: What is the longitudinal sequence of retinal ganglion cell layer thinning versus outer nuclear layer loss on spectral-domain OCT in pre-symptomatic FDXR mutation carriers?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether photoreceptor loss precedes or follows optic nerve axon degeneration will resolve whether FDXR-associated oculopathy begins as a primary rod-cone dystrophy or an ascending/descending neuro-retinal degeneration.
